001_N: ["It's three in the morning, and you're slicing a bagel in the hospital break room. The knife slips.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
002_N: ["Half an inch of your finger is just... gone.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
003_N: ["You're a doctor. You know exactly what to do. Ice, gauze, call the surgeon. But before you can move, your finger starts to itch.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
004_N: ["Then it grows. Bone, then skin, then a tiny new nail. Forty seconds. Not even a scar.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
005_N: ["The night nurse drops her coffee. You drop the bagel.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
006_N: ["So what if you could regrow any part of your body?",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
007_N: ["Sounds impossible? Not for everyone. An axolotl, a smiling little salamander from Mexico, can regrow a leg, part of its heart, even pieces of its brain. Without a single scar.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
008_N: ["In eighteen ninety-eight, scientist Thomas Hunt Morgan cut a flatworm into tiny pieces. A piece just one two-hundred-seventy-ninth of the worm grew into a whole new worm.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
010_N: ["First, you need to know how it works. So you do what any scientist would do. You experiment on yourself.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
011_N: ["Your colleague, Dr. Reyes, takes a tiny slice of skin from your arm, then stitches the wound shut, nice and neat.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
012_N: ["Nothing happens. A week later, you just have a scar.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
013_N: ["So she takes another slice, and this time leaves the wound open under a bandage. Twenty seconds later, the skin is back.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
014_N: ["Rule number one: a stitched wound scars. An open one regrows.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
015_N: ["Weirdly, real doctors noticed something similar. In nineteen seventy-four, Dr. Cynthia Illingworth in Sheffield reported that children's cut-off fingertips often grew back, if surgeons just left them alone instead of stitching them closed.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
016_N: ["It works in kids up to about eleven years old. Nail, fingerprint and all.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
017_N: ["Rule number two shows up at lunch. You're starving. You eat two burgers, a pizza, and half the vending machine.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
018_N: ["A new body part has to be built from something, and that something is whatever you eat. Every regrowth costs you a mountain of food.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
019_N: ["Rule number three shows up at a softball game. A ball knocks out your front tooth. By dinner, a new one has pushed in.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
020_N: ["Not a copy of the old tooth. A brand-new one. No filling, no stains. Whatever regrows comes back factory new.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
021_N: ["Real scientists are chasing this exact trick. In twenty twenty-four, doctors in Kyoto began the first human trial of a drug meant to help people grow new teeth. They hope it could reach patients around twenty thirty.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
022_N: ["Now, a doctor who can regrow anything starts asking a dangerous question. What else could I give away?",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
023_N: ["Here's a real fact: the human liver regrows. A living donor can give part of theirs to a patient, and in about two months it grows back to almost full size.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
025_N: ["So you become a donor. A slice of liver in March. Another in April. By December, you've given away more than one whole liver, and you're still using yours.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
026_N: ["Then you try a kidney. A normal kidney can't regrow at all. Yours is back in four days.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
027_N: ["The waiting list at your hospital gets shorter every week. The newspapers call you \"the Spare Parts Doctor.\"",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
028_N: ["And companies come calling. A man in a very expensive suit offers you a billion dollars for a vial of your cells.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
029_N: ["Real labs are already trying to grow body parts. In two thousand six, Dr. Anthony Atala reported seven young patients living with bladders grown from their own cells.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
030_N: ["And in twenty twenty-two, a young woman in Texas received an ear that was 3D-printed from her own cartilage cells.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
031_N: ["But real labs are slow, and you're not. You turn down the man in the suit. You've got patients waiting.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
032_N: ["Then, one Tuesday, Dr. Reyes looks at your blood test and goes quiet.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
033_N: ["Your cells are dividing faster than anything she's ever seen. Faster than a deer antler.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
034_N: ["Antlers are one of the fastest-growing tissues of any mammal. Up to two centimeters a day.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
035_N: ["And in twenty nineteen, scientists found that antlers grow using genes that look a lot like the genes of bone cancer. The deer just know how to keep them in check.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
036_N: ["Fast growth and cancer are two sides of the same coin. In nineteen eighty-six, a doctor named Harold Dvorak described tumors as \"wounds that do not heal.\"",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
037_N: ["\"Every time you regrow something,\" Reyes says, \"you roll the dice.\"",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
038_N: ["You start counting. Forty-one regrowths. Forty-one rolls of the dice.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
039_N: ["Three weeks later, you find it. A small, hard lump on your forearm, right where that second slice of skin grew back.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
040_N: ["Your hands shake while Reyes cuts it out. It isn't cancer. Not yet. It's just skin that didn't know when to stop.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
041_N: ["This time, she stitches the wound shut. On purpose. A scar is a stop sign.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
042_N: ["Maybe that's why we scar at all. One theory says mammals traded regrowing for something faster and safer: a quick patch that stops infection, and keeps runaway growth in check.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
043_N: ["So you decide to stop. No more regrowing. Ever.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
044_N: ["And that's exactly when Lily arrives. She's seven. Her liver is failing, and there's no donor for her on the list.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
045_N: ["Except you. Same blood type. A perfect match.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
046_N: ["A normal donor would grow that piece back over a couple of months. You'll grow it back in one night. Another roll of the dice.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
047_N: ["Reyes sits down next to you in the empty cafeteria. \"You don't owe anyone this,\" she says.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
048_N: ["You look at the bagel on your tray. The same kind that started all of this.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
050_N: ["The surgery takes nine hours. By morning, Lily's new liver is working. And yours has already grown back.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
051_N: ["For a week, you check your skin every morning. No lumps. The counter stops at forty-two. And that's where you leave it.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
052_N: ["Here's the twist, though. You don't need a superpower to regrow body parts. You already can. A little.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
053_N: ["Your liver regrows. Your skin keeps replacing itself. A broken bone rebuilds itself, and a rib can even grow back, if surgeons leave its outer lining in place.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
054_N: ["Cut nerves regrow too, about a millimeter a day. And kids' fingertips grow back, if we just leave them alone.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
055_N: ["The power isn't missing. It's switched off. And scientists are looking for the switch.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
056_N: ["In twenty twenty-two, a team led by Michael Levin at Tufts University put a tiny dome filled with five drugs over a frog's cut leg, for just twenty-four hours. Over the next eighteen months, the frog regrew a working leg.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
057_N: ["It wasn't perfect. But a frog that shouldn't regrow a leg did. And mammals are next on the list.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
058_N: ["A year later, Lily is back in your ER. She caught her finger in a car door. The tip is gone.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
059_N: ["The surgeon on duty reaches for the needle and thread. You stop him. \"Leave it open. Just a dressing.\"",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
060_N: ["Eight weeks later, Lily shows you a brand-new fingertip. Nail and all. No superpower needed.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
061_N: ["So if you could regrow one body part, which one would you pick? Tell me in the comments.",{"fish":"802e3bc2b27e49c2995d23ef70e6ac89"}]
